fiscalite.supplier.title: Small supplier threshold
fiscalite.supplier.quarterOver: Over $30,000 in a single quarter: you must register and charge taxes starting with the sale that puts you over.
fiscalite.supplier.over: Over the limit across four quarters: register for GST/QST (Revenu Québec handles both) within the following month.
fiscalite.supplier.under: Sales over the last four quarters (current one included). Above $30,000, GST/QST registration becomes mandatory.
fiscalite.tips.title: Good to know
fiscalite.tips.disclaimer: General rules, not professional advice: have an accountant check your final return.
fiscalite.tips.senc.partnersTaxed: The partnership doesn't pay income tax: its profit is split between the partners (RL-15), and each adds it to their income along with QPP and QPIP. Each of you should set aside 25 to 30% of your share.
fiscalite.tips.senc.drawings: Drawings aren't an expense: it's your share of the profits going out. Tax is based on your share of the profit, drawn or not.
fiscalite.tips.senc.paidByMe: An expense you paid out of pocket for the partnership: mark it "Paid by" you; the partnership deducts it and owes it to you. An expense you keep for yourself, you deduct it yourself (line 9943).
fiscalite.tips.senc.agreement: A written partnership agreement (shares, who does what, a partner leaving) will save you a lot of arguments.
fiscalite.tips.societe.ownTax: The corporation pays its own income tax (around 12% in Québec with the small business deduction, if it qualifies). You're taxed on what you pay yourself.
fiscalite.tips.societe.salaryDividends: Salary or dividends: salary means QPP contributions and T4/RL-1 slips to file; dividends are simpler but don't contribute. That's THE question to ask your accountant.
fiscalite.tips.societe.noPersonal: Don't pay personal expenses from the corporation's account: it becomes a taxable benefit.
fiscalite.tips.individuelle.setAside: Your profit adds to your other income, and you pay both halves of QPP (≈ 12.8%) plus QPIP. Set aside 25 to 30% of your profit.
fiscalite.tips.individuelle.bankAccount: A separate bank account for the business makes all of this much simpler.
fiscalite.tips.individuelle.homeOffice: Home office: deductible in proportion to floor area, but only down to zero profit.
fiscalite.tips.registered.notYourMoney: GST/QST collected ≠ your money: set it aside as soon as you're paid. You remit the difference with what you paid on purchases (ITCs/ITRs).
fiscalite.tips.registered.supplierNumber: To claim the taxes on a purchase of $100 or more, the invoice must show the supplier's GST/QST number.
fiscalite.tips.smallSupplier.voluntary: Small supplier: you don't charge taxes, and the ones you pay are part of your expenses. Registering voluntarily can be worth it if you buy a lot of equipment.
fiscalite.tips.keepReceipts: Keep every invoice and receipt for 6 years: that's exactly what this folder does.
